A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WARP research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplied appendices are readable and can be matched reliably across the reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original WARP experiments on image completion, electricity forecasting, dynamical systems and classification, together with original appendix analyses and ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds traffic forecasting, synthetic in-context learning, positional-encoding ablations and computational measurements.

M1.justification: The recurrence, initialization, losses, training modes and WARP-Phys variant are retained. v2 extends decoder inputs with coordinate and positional encodings, adds convolutional preprocessing for traffic forecasting, and introduces cumulative-sum processing and final-root-network reuse for in-context learning. These are targeted extensions of the existing architecture.

E1.justification: v2 adds PEMS08 traffic-network forecasting and synthetic in-context learning of linear mappings from random key-value pairs. These substantially expand the represented domains and task requirements. Earlier coverage remains, including Fashion MNIST, Spirals and high-resolution CelebA already present in v1's appendices.

E2.justification: v2 adds reported comparisons against GMAN, D2STGNN and STIDGCN on PEMS08, with baseline scores attributed to prior work (Table 2). Its new MNIST efficiency comparison also includes a Transformer alongside GRU, LSTM and S4 (Table 13). The earlier benchmark comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: UEA experiments now evaluate WARP with positional encodings. New protocols include 12-step-to-12-step traffic forecasting, length-32 in-context learning, and efficiency measurements with batch sizes 128 for MNIST and 32 for UEA. Figure 17 also specifies positional encoding for high-resolution CelebA, although Appendix D.1 says only UEA uses it, leaving that particular setting internally inconsistent.

E4.justification: v2 adds a positional-encoding ablation across six UEA datasets and computational-efficiency analyses (Tables 13–14 and 16). It revises the high-resolution CelebA case study and removes v1 Figure 13's depth-versus-width analysis of root-network weight usage. Most earlier ablations are retained and consolidated in Appendix E.5.

E5.justification: Both versions retain five-run UEA averages with plus/minus values and the specified three-run image and ETT protocols. No changed run counts, seed practices, confidence intervals or significance-testing procedures are reported. Additional positional-encoding rows use the existing uncertainty-reporting convention.

E6.justification: v2 reports results for WARP with positional encoding, including 70.93% on Worms versus v1's 60.98%; the original UEA row remains as the without-encoding condition in Table 16. PEMS08 results of MAE 6.59 and RMSE 10.10, ICL plots, efficiency measurements and revised image examples are added. Most earlier benchmark values remain unchanged. v2 Tables 4 and 16 disagree on the encoded model's Ethanol and Heartbeat scores, leaving those exact results unresolved.

T1.justification: The two convolution theorems, their assumptions and proofs are unchanged between v1 Appendix A.2 and v2 Appendix B.2.2. v2 adds mathematical definitions of pixel and sinusoidal coordinates and an algebraic equivalence argument supporting cumulative-sum ICL and reuse of the learned mapping (Section 3.4), providing a limited mathematical extension.

C1.justification: v2 promotes in-context learning to an explicit core capability and contribution. Its abstract and introduction strengthen the classification claim to top-three performance on five of six UEA datasets. The contribution narrative shifts toward these real-world and ICL capabilities; WARP-Phys and its large MSD advantage already existed in v1 despite their increased prominence.

C2.justification: v1 attributes weak EigenWorms/Motor results to vanishing gradients and labels high-resolution CelebA a failure case. v2 instead attributes improved long-sequence behavior to initialization and positional encoding and presents revised CelebA examples as evidence of suitability. It removes the imputation/control extension discussion and adds a qualification that JAX/PyTorch implementation differences can affect efficiency comparisons.

D1.justification: v1 already documents architectures, optimization, hardware and training budgets. v2 adds UEA positional-encoding dimensions and frequency constants (Table 10), traffic input and convolution specifications, ICL input-format instructions, and resource profiles with JIT-compilation exclusions. These extend the existing reproducibility information; the stated code/data access location is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 substantially expands connections to fast weights, delta-rule updates, test-time training and amortized inference, including new citations to Schmidhuber, MesaNet and Test-time Training Done Right. It adds a Koopman-operator perspective and associated references, plus ICL and traffic literature. Rumelhart et al. (1986) is removed. These changes extend the research positioning beyond the relocation of related work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, architecture explanations and discussion are substantially rewritten. Related work moves to Appendix A, main-text ablation material is consolidated in Appendix E.5, and ICL becomes main Section 3.4. Appendix organization, terminology, algorithm notation and author/header text also change.

P2.justification: v2 adds an unfolded-model diagram, comparative MNIST examples, ICL pipeline/results plots, and traffic, positional-encoding and efficiency tables. Existing plots are split, merged and relocated; algorithm figures become numbered algorithms, the depth/width figure is removed, and high-resolution CelebA examples are replaced. The page template and display arrangement also change throughout.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides useful positional-encoding controls, broader empirical coverage and clearer implementation and resource documentation. However, new inconsistencies undermine important conclusions: Tables 4 and 16 give different encoded-model accuracies for Ethanol (36.49 versus 32.91) and Heartbeat (80.65 versus 88.65), while Table 13 calls WARP fastest despite listing 45.22 seconds per epoch against the Transformer's 18.62. The PDFs do not resolve these discrepancies, preventing a reliable judgment that the added evidence and clarity outweigh the reduced consistency.
